response.text:
Cropping has clear precedents, but different supervision semantics. [CL4SRec](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2010.14395) randomly selects a contiguous subsequence of length ⌊ηL⌋; it need not retain the latest interaction. Two augmented histories supply a contrastive objective alongside next-item prediction, so cropped views do not inherently require next-item labels. Its augmentation-only ablation helps separate augmentation from contrastive learning, but does not establish stale-interest removal. [CoSeRec](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2108.06479) retains cropping while adding correlation-aware substitution/insertion; it excludes crop/reorder for short histories to avoid excessive information loss. These are primarily Transformer results, not direct evidence for GRU-specific recency benefits.

A recurrent precedent is [Tan et al. (2016)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1606.08117): expand sessions into all prefix/next-item pairs, then apply stochastic embedding dropout to input histories while retaining labels. Prefix expansion increases supervised instances; stochastic corruption supplies regularization. Their temporal adaptation separately fine-tunes on recent sessions. [CausalRec’s CausalBoost paper](https://arxiv.org/html/2510.21333v1) instead learns causal structure to refine attention; it is not a direct suffix-cropping precedent.

For suffix cropping, the target-preserving construction is (xₛ,…,xₜ) → xₜ₊₁: remove only earlier context, retain the endpoint and original target, and keep targets outside inputs. Recommended controls—not established findings from these papers—are full history, deterministic recent suffix, stochastic suffix, and equal-length random crops, with identical target sampling, optimizer updates, negatives, and loss normalization. For per-position GRU training, match active target counts or report changes explicitly. Deterministic versus stochastic suffixes tests added regularization; length-matched crops test endpoint recency, although arbitrary crops paired with the original target introduce a prediction gap. Thus suffix cropping alone offers limited novelty; a stale-interest explanation requires controlled evidence.
